3.2 mm normal length and 3.2 mm short length burner tubes will be manifested and used for BASS.
The Control Box will be modified to allow the fan flow adjustment to stop the fan when set to its minimum 
as a safety mechanism to extinguish flame.
Parameter Measurement
Measurement of the GN2 Flow rate, Fan Voltage, Co-Flow velocity, and flame radiation will be measured and overlaid on the video.
The data acquisition rate as measured by SPICE hardware is 4 Hz.
The measurement accuracy of ±10% was met by the SPICE hardware prior to its launch.  The measurement accuracy will meet the requirements for BASS.
Imaging Requirements
The Field of view of the video is fixed for BASS can not be changed from SPICE.
The Still Image requirements are the same as for SPICE.  The BASS still image requirements will be met with the Nikon model D300s digital still camera.
4/14/2010

BASS Engineering Requirements
Acceleration
BASS testing will be scheduled around planned thruster firing or spacecraft dock or undock
.
The acceleration environment will be measured by the Space Acceleration Measurement System (SAMS) during BASS testing which will be installed into the Microgravity Science 
Glovebox
 (MSG) Work Volume.
Oxygen Concentration
The BASS experiment will include steps in crew procedures to install a Compound Specific Analyzer (CSA-O2) into the MSG to measure the Oxygen concentration.  There is also a 
Major Constituent Analyzer 
available to measure the Columbus Module concentration. 
Crew inserts fuel sample and adjusts igniter and fuel base to desired position
Sample Frame Assembly is designed to allow for adjustment of the position of the BASS solid fuel sample.
The Igniter has a wire extension that the crew will be able to position as required to ignite the solid fuel sample.

BASS Science Objectives
Objective:
Bridge the gap between normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test # 1 method, ground based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity.
Test effectiveness of an inert, gaseous extinguishing agent 
(nitrogen, similar 
to that used on 
the International Space Station 
(
ISS
) in putting out flames over different materials, geometries, and flow.
Relevance/Impact:
Relationship between ground test and microgravity test can be investigated by observing flames burning for longer times.
Practical, realistic fuels in typical geometries will be examined, including wake flames which 
have characteristics of a fire burning behind another object.
Development Approach:
BASS will utilize the on orbit hardware SPICE which was launched on STS-126 and operates on 
the International Space Station (ISS) in the Microgravity Science 
Glovebox
 (MSG
) facility.
Crew required to set up and operate the experiment.  
BASS experiment data is captured on video and still camera 
data 
then down-linked 
to the ground for 
evaluation by the science team.

BASS Success Criteria
Minimal Success:
 20 total tests including: eight tests with flat samples (four materials at two different flow speeds); four tests with spherical PMMA samples (four different flow speeds with nitrogen extinguishment); four tests with candles (four different flow speeds with nitrogen extinguishment); and four tests of PMMA wake flames (four different flow speeds with nitrogen extinguishment). 
Complete Success:
 60 flames as indicated in test matrix.
